content.title: Chuck Norris Quietly Built a Surprising Business Empire
content.text: The Walker, Texas Ranger star built a sprawling business empire—from karate studios to bottled water—long before his final bow. Chuck Norris. Photo: Getty ImagesListen to this ArticleMore info0:00 / 0:00Chuck Norris, best known for his work as an action star on Walker Texas Ranger’ died today at age 86. While most know him as a Hollywood star, he also built an impressive business empire.The entrepreneur and martial artist expanded into multiple business ventures as well as dabbling in philanthropy. The Norris family confirmed the actor’s death in a statement on Friday. “He lived his life with faith, purpose, and an unwavering commitment to the people he loved. Through his work, discipline, and kindness, he inspired millions around the world and left a lasting impact on so many lives,” the statement read.Chuck Norris’ Net WorthBefore his passing, Norris’ net worth in 2026 was estimated at $70 million which came from a wide mix revenue streams, according to Celebrity Net Worth. A major driver of that financial success comes from his time on Walker, Texas Ranger, playing the show’s titular character. It ran for 9 seasons and roughly 200 episodes pulling in 10+ million weekly viewers by season 6. In court documents obtained by The Hollywood Reporter, from a 2019 lawsuit brought by Norris’ Top Kick Productions, the series has amassed more than $692 million in revenue since its debut. Norris not only was the shows main star, but also an executive producer who amassed a significant ownership stake in the show. The exact percentage has never been disclosed to the public. Business RootsLong before Walker, Texas Ranger, Norris had already established himself as a businessman. After receiving an honorable discharge from the Air Force in 1962, he opened several Chuck Norris Karate Studios, attracting students including celebrities like Priscilla Presley.
